excluded_items.mi_chunkbin_t: M7: the `mi_stats_t` chunk-bin enumeration of the statistics profile, not an allocation operation.
excluded_items.mi_commit_fun_t: M6: the commit callback type of `mi_manage_os_memory_ex` managed memory.
excluded_items.mi_malloc_size: M8: defined only by src/alloc-override.c under MI_MALLOC_OVERRIDE, the owned-libc `malloc_size`/`malloc_usable_size` override integration.
excluded_items.mi_malloc_usable_size: M8: defined only by src/alloc-override.c under MI_MALLOC_OVERRIDE, the owned-libc `malloc_usable_size` override integration.

differential:operations.scope: One checked-in C driver runs as two separate processes, linked once against the pinned C v3.5.0 release sources and once against the native adapter, and both address-free traces (logical ids, reuse relations, usable size, alignment, 64 KiB slice) must be equal: allocation, zeroing, calloc/mallocn overflow, usable and good size across every size class, the realloc family (ceil-half reuse, grow/shrink copy, rezalloc/recalloc tail zeroing, reallocf release, reallocarray/reallocarr errno), expand, the aligned family (natural, over-allocated, offset, OS-aligned singleton, invalid alignment, meta alignment), posix_memalign/memalign/valloc/pvalloc/aligned_alloc argument rules, umalloc/urealloc/ufree block sizes, the free forms and mi_cfree/mi_check_owned, the strdup/realpath/dupenv conveniences with errno after each call, and identical termination of the plain-C mi_new abort cases.

differential:page-kinds.scope: Separate pinned-C and native-adapter processes run the same driver scenario: for request sizes at each small, medium, large, and huge-singleton edge, two pages' worth of blocks (so pages fill and leave their queue), interleaved frees, and a second round whose blocks, slices, and reuse relations show the page selection, retirement, and release of each kind.

differential:collection.scope: Separate pinned-C and native-adapter processes run the same driver scenario: after filling and freeing pages of several classes, `mi_collect(false)`, `mi_collect(true)`, or no collection, then a different-class probe and a same-class allocation whose block, slice, and reuse relations show which pages each collection released.

differential:oom-failure.scope: Under a fixed RLIMIT_AS both processes refuse the same OS-backed requests: NULL results and errno for malloc/calloc/aligned/realloc/posix_memalign, preservation of the old block and its bytes on realloc and aligned-realloc failure, reallocf release, continued service from existing pages, and recovery after the limit is lifted.

unit:native-operations.scope: The focused native-engine integration regressions for aligned and ordinary reallocation, owner-local and foreign reallocation, pointer-first usable size, and huge-singleton local free.

adapter:export-boundary.scope: The native adapter builds as a static library whose defined `mi_*` globals include every M4 external function and only functions the pinned header declares, that defines no libc allocator entry and no C mimalloc `_mi_*` internal, and against which alone a C probe naming every function through the pinned `include/mimalloc.h` prototypes links and runs on native x86-64.

upstream:test-api.scope: Unmodified pinned `test/test-api.c` with `testhelper.h` compiles against the pinned headers, links against the native adapter only, and every M4-owned check reports `ok.` (the heap-os1, heap-os2, heap-many, and arena_reserve checks belong to M6).

differential:threads.scope: Separate pinned-C and native-adapter processes run the same threaded driver scenario: a worker bound by its first call allocates, reallocates an initial-thread block in place through the shared Heap, frees an initial-thread huge block remotely, and exits; the initial thread then reallocates and frees the exited worker's blocks and observes the resulting reuse; a second worker's first call is `mi_malloc_aligned(0, 16)` (test-api.c `zero_aligned_first`).

gates.acceptance: Default-Theap allocation follows src/alloc.c: `mi_malloc(0)` returns a distinct minimal block, an oversized request still counts its generic call and forces one collection before failing, overflowing counts fail without a message, zeroing entries return zeroed usable bytes, the `u` forms report the page block size, and the `mi_new` family follows the plain-C `mi_try_new_handler` (abort unless nothrow). errno is the default error handler's result; message rendering and registered handlers are M7's error-reporting sites.

Every free form reaches src/free.c `mi_free_nonnull` after the PageMap lookup (NULL and unmapped pointers are no-ops; the sized and aligned forms ignore their hints in release), `mi_cfree` frees only a pointer `_mi_checked_ptr_page` maps and reports whether it did, and `mi_ufree` reports the freed page block size (0 when unmapped).

Reallocation follows `mi_theap_realloc_zero_ex`: NULL allocates, zero size returns a zero-initialized minimal block, ceil-half same-Heap reuse, copy of min(old usable, new size), zeroing of the source tail range, the old block survives every failure, and the alloc-posix.c errno rules; `mi_expand` never moves.

Aligned allocation follows src/alloc-aligned.c: power-of-two validation, the small free-head fast path, natural alignment, over-allocation with interior pointers through MI_PAGE_MAX_OVERALLOC_ALIGN, OS-aligned singletons above it (offset refused), `pointer + offset` alignment for the `_at` forms, the aligned ceil-half reuse predicate and tail zeroing for reallocation, and the alloc-posix.c `posix_memalign`/`memalign`/`aligned_alloc` rules.

`mi_usable_size` follows `_mi_usable_size` (NULL and unowned pointers report 0, interior aligned pointers report the adjusted extent) and `mi_good_size` returns the source bin or OS-page rounding for every request, including requests above MI_MAX_ALLOC_SIZE.

The alloc.c and alloc-posix.c conveniences allocate through the default Theap with the source length limits, errno results (`mi_wdupenv_s` is EINVAL on Linux), `mi_path_max` realpath buffer, OS-page `valloc`/`pvalloc` rounding, `mi_is_redirected` false, and `mi_check_owned` answering `mi_any_heap_contains` from the safe PageMap lookup.

`mi_collect(force)` runs `mi_theap_collect_ex` on the calling thread's default Theap: retired-page and deferred collection, abandoned-page and free-list collection, freeing empty pages, and with `force` the arena purge and forced reclamation the source performs.
Small, medium, large, and huge-singleton pages are selected at the source size-class boundaries and freed back through their owners, with the same block sizes, alignments, and reuse as pinned C.

OS refusal propagates as the source NULL/errno result without corrupting allocator state, and every failed reallocation preserves the old block and its bytes (`reallocf` releases it). `mi_option_retry_on_oom` is a Windows-only retry and has no Linux effect.

One native adapter exports every M4 external function, and only pinned-header functions, with the pinned `mimalloc.h` prototypes over `__crabc_runtime`, attaches and finishes threads through the source thread-done key, and contains no C mimalloc object.
The unmodified pinned `test/test-api.c` passes every M4-owned check through the native adapter.
blocked_by: The unmodified file cannot link against a native adapter: beyond the M4 exports it references `mi_option_disable` (M7), `mi_reserve_os_memory`, `mi_heap_new`, `mi_heap_malloc`, `mi_heap_malloc_aligned`, `mi_heap_delete`, `mi_heap_destroy` (M6), and `mi_stats_get` (M7).
